content: Yazdī collection items 3 and 4: two letters from Khwāja Jamāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Turka, called son of Yazdī's teacher Ibn Turka (makhdūmzāda-yi ḥaqīqī; MK's footnote says he may instead be a son of Afżal al-Dīn Turka), before Shaʿbān 867/May 1463, one to Amīr Muḥammad Shāh, governor (dārūghā) of Isfahan and brother of Fīrūzshāh, the other to the late Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad Ṭāhir. They show him struggling to finish his education: sent to Shiraz from Herat, perhaps in adolescence, he fears that going back to Herat would end his studies because of his ties and duties there (YMN/V ff. 139a-40b).
